title: Reuse d_tag slot for kind:30443 publishes to enable NIP-33 replacement
body:
## Summary

Implements d_tag reuse for MLS key package (kind:30443) publishes so that successive key package rotations replace the previous event on relays per NIP-33, rather than accumulating as distinct addressable events.

The MDK library generates a fresh random `d` tag on every `create_key_package_for_event()` call, but its documentation explicitly states: "Callers SHOULD store and reuse this value when rotating the KeyPackage." Without reuse, relays accumulate stale key packages indefinitely instead of replacing them.

## Key Changes

- **New helper function `apply_d_tag_override()`**: Conditionally swaps the freshly-generated `d` tag from MDK with a previously-stored one, preserving all other event tags (MLS metadata, ciphersuite, extensions, etc.)

- **Database layer (`published_key_packages.rs`)**: Added `find_latest_d_tag()` method to retrieve the most recently recorded `d` tag for a given event kind, ordered by creation time with fallback to ID ordering

- **Repository wrapper**: Exposed `find_latest_d_tag()` through the `PublishedKeyPackagesRepo` interface for session-based access

- **Key package publish flow**: Modified `publish_key_package_for_account_with_signer()` to:
  - Query the database for any previously-stored `d` tag before publishing
  - Apply the override if found (gracefully falls back to fresh d_tag on query failure)
  - Pass canonical tags and d_tag to the relay publish and database record operations

- **Comprehensive test coverage**:
  - Unit tests for `apply_d_tag_override()` covering both stored and fresh d_tag paths
  - Unit tests for `find_latest_d_tag()` with empty table, multiple rows, and kind filtering
  - Integration test verifying that successive key package publishes reuse the same d_tag slot across multiple publish cycles

## Implementation Details

- The override is applied at the event-building stage, before relay publication and database recording, ensuring consistency across all downstream operations
- Error handling is defensive: if the d_tag lookup fails, the system logs a warning and falls back to the fresh MDK-generated d_tag rather than failing the publish
- The database query uses `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` to handle both normal ordering and edge cases where multiple rows share the same timestamp
- All non-d tags are preserved unchanged to maintain MLS validation and metadata integrity

title: Recover some coverage on account DB wrappers and membership ops
body:
## Summary

The arch-refactor merge dropped CI coverage 94.95% → 89.02%. This PR adds 8 targeted unit tests covering paths the refactor introduced without tests — three new per-account-DB repositories and the lightweight column-flip behavior of `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive` / `unarchive`.

## What's tested

`database/account/push_registrations.rs` (2 tests)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_registration` — the wrapper's only added behavior is binding `account_pubkey`; this locks it in.
- `separate_accounts_have_independent_per_account_dbs` — the per-account-DB architectural invariant (post-#786 split); two repos over distinct account DBs must not see each other's rows. Inner `PushRegistration` tests share one pool and can't express this.

`database/account/group_push_tokens.rs` (1 test)
- `upsert_binds_repo_account_pubkey_to_returned_token` — pubkey-binding contract on the wrapper.

`database/account/published_key_packages.rs` (1 test)
- `mark_key_material_deleted_by_id_flips_one_row_only` — contrapositive regression guard for PR #822: the by-id variant must NOT cascade to dual-kind twins. A future refactor that "fixes consistency" by accidentally hash_ref-scoping the by-id variant trips this test. No inner-test analogue.

`accounts_groups.rs` (4 tests)
- `test_archive_sets_archived_at`, `test_archive_is_idempotent`, `test_unarchive_clears_archived_at`, `test_unarchive_on_unarchived_chat_is_no_op` — lightweight column-flip tests for `MembershipOpsForGroup::archive`/`unarchive` via the `get_or_create(None)` path. Distinct from the existing `chat_list.rs` archive tests, which spin up a real MLS group via `create_group(...)` and assert stream emit; these target the wrapper's mutation contract without the MLS setup cost.

## What's deliberately not in this PR

- **Wrapper pure-delegation roundtrip tests.** Pure pass-through `Ok(Inner::fn(...).await?)` calls add coverage but no signal — the inner SQL has its own tests. Per the user rule "tests that really increase coverage, not tests that are not testing anything," these were dropped after review.
- **Hash_ref-scoped twin tests** for `mark_consumed` / `mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref`. Already covered by the inner tests `test_mark_consumed_updates_timestamp_for_twins` and `test_mark_key_material_deleted_by_hash_ref_marks_twins` in `database/published_key_packages.rs`.
- **Archive/unarchive emit-frame tests.** Already covered at the heavyweight level by `test_archive_chat_emits_to_both_stream_channels` in `chat_list.rs`.
- **Schema-shadowing fix.** The account-DB tests currently hand-roll a `DROP TABLE + CREATE TABLE` because `AccountDatabase::new` uses `open_without_migrations` (running the full timeline here would require wiring a shared pool). Filed for a separate follow-up — a `setup_account_db_with_migrations()` helper that the whole `account/*.rs` suite can migrate to.

## Coverage math caveat

Coverage probably lands around 90–92% local lib — clears the post-merge CI baseline of 89.02% but doesn't recover the full pre-merge 94.95%. The remaining gap is structural: arch-refactor genuinely deleted code paths that had coverage, and shallow tests aren't the right fix.

## Verification

- `just check-fmt` ✓
- `just check-clippy` ✓
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::database::account` — 55 pass
- `cargo test --lib whitenoise::accounts_groups::tests` — all pass including the 4 new archive/unarchive

title: feat: add whitenoise-markdown crate and retire nostr-sdk token parser
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/118ef3460c2a0e43c2761573bf407aa1c865ca8db8d0ff76938fb375cd710d02.png)

Adds a Markdown layer for chat content and retires the nostr-sdk token parser. This is a full Abstract Syntax Tree, not just yet another markdown to html converter or anything of the sort.

> [!IMPORTANT] 
> I know it looks like a ton of code, but it's mostly tests, and I want to keep them. I don't want this to fail in the app because something wasn't tested properly.

The diff outside the new crate is a net **-384 lines** (96 added, 480 removed). Inside the new `whitenoise-markdown` crate, tests are about 4.9k lines vs ~3.1k of source. The big number on the PR page is test coverage, not code we have to maintain forever.

## What changed

**New crate: `crates/whitenoise-markdown`**
Hand-written CommonMark + GFM + nostr-extension parser. One optional dep (`serde`). Emits a typed AST: blocks (headings, lists, blockquotes, tables, code/math), inlines (emphasis, links, autolinks, code, math), plus two nostr node types for bare `@npub1...` mentions and explicit `nostr:<hrp>1...` URIs. `nsec` is rejected.

**Migration: nostr-sdk tokens to Markdown AST**
- `ChatMessage.content_tokens` is now a `Document` (was `Vec<SerializableToken>`).
- `MessageWithTokens.tokens` is now a `Document`. Field name kept the same for FFI continuity.
- The aggregator no longer takes a `parser: &dyn Parser` argument. It calls `whitenoise_markdown::parse` directly.
- `nostr_manager::parser` (`ContentParser`, `SerializableToken`, the `Parser` trait, `MockParser`) is deleted.
- The DB layer derives the AST from `content` on read instead of persisting a stale token vec.

**Golden tests**
`crates/whitenoise-markdown/tests/golden/` holds 4 paired `.md` and `.json` fixtures covering the kitchen sink (every CommonMark and GFM feature), tables and math, nested containers, and a nostr-heavy document. The runner asserts byte-exact match of `serde_json::to_string_pretty(&doc)`. To refresh after intentional parser changes:

```
WHITENOISE_MD_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p whitenoise-markdown --test golden
```

On mismatch, the failure prints the first differing line and the regenerate command.

## Caveats

The golden JSON captures two current parser behaviors worth a second look later: 

1. trailing content sometimes hoists out of its container
2. two source-distinct bullet lists separated by paragraphs can fold into one. 

The tests lock these in, so any fix will surface as a reviewable diff.

I also chose not to support admonitions, if we want those I can add them in a follow up PR. 

## Worth a marmot

The colony now reads Markdown.

title: Investigate slow initial startup time (~15s)
body:
## Context

Initial app startup currently feels too slow. The observed startup time is roughly 15 seconds before the app is ready.

This issue is to investigate where that time is being spent inside `whitenoise-rs` initialization and startup work.

## Details

Areas that look worth profiling first:

- `Whitenoise::initialize_whitenoise()` overall startup path
- startup cache sync work such as `sync_message_cache_on_startup()`
- relay / control-plane initialization
- scheduled task startup
- database migrations or other one-time initialization work
- any blocking network calls or waits happening before the UI can proceed

Questions to answer:

- what are the biggest contributors to the ~15 second startup time
- how much of that cost is local CPU / I/O vs network waiting
- which work is truly required before the app becomes usable
- which work can be deferred until after first render / first usable state
- whether there is a measurable difference between first startup, cold startup, and subsequent launches

## Outcome

Produce a breakdown of startup cost and identify concrete follow-up optimizations.

Possible outcomes:

- move non-critical startup work off the critical path
- defer sync or maintenance tasks until after initial readiness
- add instrumentation / timing logs around initialization phases
- split one-time setup from normal launch work
- open targeted follow-up issues once the hotspots are known

## Additional context

There is already app-side DX work around startup behavior in `marmot-protocol/whitenoise`, but this issue is specifically about the Rust core initialization path because that is likely where a large part of the delay lives.

title: feat(frb): move FRB codegen into whitenoise-rs
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/0d80f60e49ed191332de5c793af8dcd359ddbaafadfb1502bee89aff427dff4d.jpg)

## What changes

Replaces the force-pushed `flutter-package` orphan branch with a Dart pub registry served from this repo's `gh-pages` branch. The Flutter app consumes it via a standard `hosted:` pubspec source.

Master now owns the full Flutter package template at `crates/whitenoise-frb/template/`. The wrapper crate and Dart package rename from `rust_lib_whitenoise` to `whitenoise_frb`, dropping the FRB-default `rust_lib_*` prefix.

## How publishing works

Each codeowner push to master triggers `.github/workflows/frb-codegen.yml`:

1. Stage the package shell from the vendored template
2. Run `flutter_rust_bridge_codegen` to produce fresh Dart bindings
3. Vendor the wrapper crate, rewriting the `whitenoise` path-dep to a git rev pinning the source SHA
4. Build a tarball plus a Pub Spec v2 version JSON
5. Apply the version to a gh-pages worktree (index update + tarball drop)
6. Commit and push gh-pages

The codeowner gate is unchanged, and concurrency serializes publishes so gh-pages stays consistent across overlapping runs.

## Versioning

Each publish gets `0.0.0-dev+<short-sha>`. Flutter pins specific versions. Per semver, build metadata after `+` does not participate in version ordering, so `version: any` would resolve arbitrarily; pin-only.

## Consuming from the Flutter app

```yaml
dependencies:
  whitenoise_frb:
    hosted: https://marmot-protocol.github.io/whitenoise-rs
    version: "0.0.0-dev+<short-sha>"
```

The latest published SHA lives at `/api/packages/whitenoise_frb` in the registry.

## Migration sequence

1. Bootstrap gh-pages and enable Pages serving (done)
2. Land this PR; first master push publishes a version
3. Land the Flutter cutover PR on `marmot-protocol/whitenoise`
4. Delete the orphan branch: `git push origin --delete flutter-package`

Full details, including the Flutter-side checklist, live in `docs/frb-flutter-migration.md`.

## Verified

- `just frb-stage && just frb-generate && just frb-check` runs end-to-end
- `just frb-publish-local` produces a spec-valid tarball
- Pages serves the bootstrap landing page at https://marmot-protocol.github.io/whitenoise-rs/

The known coverage flake (`test_interrupted_migration_restores_valid_encrypted_temp_when_database_missing`) is pre-existing; fails on both this branch and its prior commit.

---

A marmot once kept its outbound mail in a side burrow that everyone had to know the name of. Now it runs a proper post office with numbered packages on the shelf. The side burrow gets filled in once the last package ships.
